explanations: C-1. Compared with no Halvern Steel Safeguard Order, price paid for buyers.current rises from the short run onward (tier B, invisible). Why: TX-7: a tariff the foreign sellers do not absorb raises what domestic buyers pay and lets protected domestic producers charge and sell more. This holds if: Imports remain a meaningful share of supply, and foreign sellers do not absorb most of the tariff (p = 0.72). Reported.

C-2. Compared with no Halvern Steel Safeguard Order, resources available other uses for buyers.current falls from the short run onward (tier A, invisible). Why: TX-1: a tax that is collected takes resources from those who bear it and yields revenue; TX-7: a tariff the foreign sellers do not absorb raises what domestic buyers pay and lets protected domestic producers charge and sell more. This holds if: Imports remain a meaningful share of supply, and foreign sellers do not absorb most of the tariff (p = 0.72). Reported.

C-3. Compared with no Halvern Steel Safeguard Order, quantity supplied for export_industries falls from the medium run onward (tier B, invisible). Why: TX-7: a tariff the foreign sellers do not absorb raises what domestic buyers pay and lets protected domestic producers charge and sell more; TX-2: a tax on each unit opens a wedge between what buyers pay and what sellers keep, and the market shrinks; TX-8: foreigners who sell less to the country earn less of its currency and so buy fewer of its exports. This holds if: Imports remain a meaningful share of supply, and foreign sellers do not absorb most of the tariff (p = 0.72); The fall in imports is not offset by capital flows or other adjustments within the medium run (p = 0.35). Not reported: an assumption is below the 0.5 cut-off.

This holds if: Imports remain a meaningful share of supply, and foreign sellers do not absorb most of the tariff (p = 0.72). Reported.

source_sentences: Importers of record must pay a tariff of 25% of the customs value on imports of flat-rolled and long steel products, for three years.
A review in the third year may extend it.
Imported fabricated steel products and finished goods containing steel (machinery, vehicles, appliances, fabricated structural sections, fasteners) are not covered.
The Customs Service checks classification at ports and penalizes misdeclaration.
The revenue goes to the general budget.
Steel users may apply to exclude a product "not produced domestically in sufficient quantity or quality".
Decisions are due within 90 days; exclusions last one year and must be renewed.

context: Halvern is a mid-sized trading country with its own currency and a floating exchange rate.
Three domestic steel firms supply about 60% of the steel used in Halvern; the rest is imported.
About 4,000 domestic manufacturers use steel as a main input (machinery, vehicle parts, household appliances, cans, construction products); machinery makers export about 35% of their output.
Halvern's other large export industries are grain and tourism.
Halvern buys a small share of the world's steel.

readings: U1-a: 'it' is the tariff; the review may extend the 25% tariff beyond its three-year term, and no limit on the extension is stated.
U1-b: 'it' is the three-year term; the review may lengthen the term, and the tariff continues during any extension.

readings: U2-a: a product qualifies for exclusion when domestic production is insufficient in quantity or insufficient in quality (either shortfall is enough).
U2-b: a product qualifies for exclusion only when domestic production is insufficient in both quantity and quality.
